second_review.notes: Cold read of run 20261021T175809Z_staged. Source fidelity re-checked against the_symbol_game: terminal_from_fiber (terminal_status.rs 166-220) matches both fiberStatus (Lean) and the checker's valid-count/case-split classifier; checked_packet.rs 243-250 and run.rs 626-633 are as transcribed; the relRoute copy matches Routing.lean. All 33 anchors state what the profile says they state, and the profile now labels the definitional ones (diag_cannot_set_authority / diag_cannot_set_terminal are rfl on a Situation that omits diag; AuthTag has no Certified constructor; policy theorems are 3-set-to-7-set cardinality facts; exactRepairAllowed = certEligible; runTag ExactClass = none encodes 'tag is not a Pfp'). Checker: independent grouped transcription, 343-policy enumeration, determination by fibres, strict types, and it now asserts the complete public family (sorted(cases) == the 21/10/3/8/640/8 lines); records_checked = 690 matches. Earlier pass (a): every amendment is in the final text (supports 1-5, narrowest_claim, does_not_support, next_test), the sha256 pins of routing.rs, terminal_status.rs, trichotomy.rs, run.rs, checked_packet.rs, terminal_routing.json and Routing.lean are in the profile (b) the rebuild introduced no weakened check; the checker's only hard-coded data are the declared source transcriptions (shared-transcription risk is stated); the cosmetic Lean linter issue is gone; 15 semantic mutants now include the ParseRefused mistranscription, no_rule_certifiable, the tag-identification near miss and the exact-class-counted-as-routed near miss. (c) What the earlier pass missed, visible cold: (1) supports (2) says '2 of the 21 cells declared, 1 class unrouted, 19 cells neither realised nor excluded'. The 19 is just 21 - 2 (checker diag_cells = len(cells) - len(routed)); if the declared composite is read as a function on the two routed classes, the other 12 cells of those rows ARE excluded and only the 7 cells of the exact-class row are open. The wording 'neither realised nor excluded' is imprecise, not false for the unrouted row, so it is an amendment, not a rebuild. (2) 'the only source code taking a diagnostic class towards authority (checked_packet.rs:248)' (supports 4, qualification) is a universal over the source that no recorded scan backs: grep of the_symbol_game finds other consumers of ObstructionDiagnosticClass, notably omega_mub/src/runtime_adapter.rs:200-205 terminal_for(class) -> CodaTerminal (ExactRepair, StabilizedSurvivor, OpenObstruction), a total class-to-'terminal' map in another crate that the node does not model (no From<CodaTerminal> for RoutingTerminal was found by grep), and omega_certifiers/src/counterfeit_detection.rs:117,184 which branches on ExactRepair for fraud checks (a gate, not authority). The claim should say 'the only one among the files read' and list the unmodelled consumers in does_not_support. (3) 'contrary to ledger N01' is a little strong: N01 says a class is not a routing terminal, repair action, stabilisation receipt or authority and that ExactClass is not ExactRepair; the Rust variant name ExactRepair and the status-tag string StabilizedSurvivor are naming/tagging in code, which is in tension with N01 but is not shown to identify the class with the repair action. (4) The sealed model drops the Verified-certificate and replay-hash conditions of certify_evidence, so 'never sufficient' holds a fortiori; fine, but sealed is a model of line 248 only. (5) All semantic mutants are single-record edits; the shared-transcription mutants (ParseRefused, NoRule certifiable) are coordinate-style, so the real transcription risk is covered only by the unit test that re-reads the pinned Rust text, as the claim says. No wrong certificate can pass the checker: every record is recomputed from its own input fields and the full input family is enforced.

earlier_pass.notes: Checked against the real sources in the_symbol_game (routing.rs, terminal_status.rs, run.rs 626-633, checked_packet.rs 243-250, terminal_routing.json): the transcribed tables (21 statuses, From<TerminalStatus>, From<PfpTerminal>, residual_class, authority_level, authority_terminal, terminal_from_fiber order of tests) are faithful, and the checker's fibre classifier agrees with the Lean one on all 640 inputs. The machinery is sound but the claim text overstates in five places. (1) Authority: supports (4) says the diagnostic class 'is not an input' of Certified, yet checked_packet.rs:248 maps ObstructionDiagnosticClass::ExactRepair to AuthorityTerminal::ExactRuleDerived and every other class to NotAuthorityBearing; the class is a necessary eligibility gate. The Lean theorems diag_cannot_set_authority and diag_cannot_set_terminal are rfl because Situation.authority and Situation.terminal are defined without the diag field (hypothesis hidden in a definition), and AuthTag has no Certified constructor so 'never Certified' is true by type construction; the checker's authority leaf (certified = lambda s, w: w and s in bearing; producer hard-codes 0) is likewise definitional. (2) 'the only code turning a class into a terminal (run.rs tag + terminal_routing.json)': no single code does this. run.rs emits a String tag; nothing in omega_id_run references terminal_routing or PfpTerminal (grep), and terminal_routing.json is consumed by the Python omega_engine_pfp pipeline over its own statuses. diagRoute is the author's string-identity composition; Lean runTag returns none for ExactClass by definition, so diagRoute_values is a transcription check, not a derivation. (3) The policy theorems (policy_values_independent, no_value_forced, card_policies, no_surjective_policy, card_injective_policies) are facts about maps from any 3-set to any 7-set. They are not evidence about the source, and the source does determine 2 of the 3 values, so 'no value is forced' sits uneasily next to supports (2); the narrowest_claim 'no forced map between the class and the terminal' should read 'nothing forces the partial composite the source declares'. (4) The source itself violates the ledger discipline this node names: the Rust variant of the class is called ExactRepair and run.rs line 631 tags ClosedResidual as StabilizedSurvivor, the identification N01 forbids ('ClosedResidual is not StabilizedSurvivor'). The profile mentions it in source_scope_review but the narrowest_claim reads as if separation holds; exactRepairAllowed is literally identical to certEligible (both ExactClass => true), so the DAG clause 'ExactClass is not ExactRepair' has no anchor of its own. (5) Two different Rust enums are called ResidualClass: terminal_status::ResidualClass {Exact, ClosedSurvivor, Open, Refused} (the one modelled) and omega_homology::trichotomy_witness::ResidualClass {ExactRepair, StabilizedSurvivor, OpenObstruction} used in run.rs 847-855, which is isomorphic to the diagnostic class by variant name; does_not_support 'any identification of ResidualClass with the diagnostic class' must say which. Checker: strong on leaves (strict types, exact keys, fibre classifier by a different algorithm, 343 policies enumerated), but it never asserts completeness of the public input (no check that kinds/counts are 21/10/3/8/640/8), and every mutant is a single-leaf edit that recomputation rejects trivially; no mutant targets the real risk, a wrong shared transcription of a source table. next_test partly repeats does_not_support (a route for the exact class, O01) and is a design task rather than a test.
